solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rod's intelligence evident in school

indicators.note: something evident in a place is seen inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: SCH is the standard abbreviation for school
wit is quick intelligence

explanation.surface: A boy called Rod shows how clever he is at school.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Rod is just 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a thin flexible stick or cane, so it is a kind of rod.

clue.text: Ghost to appear without notice

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: to show up is to appear
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A ghost turns up unannounced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without notice' reads as 'unannounced', but 'without' means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to ghost or shadow someone is to follow them closely and secretly; as nouns both are faint phantom figures.

clue.text: Indistinguishable from variously indelicate expressions originally deleted

indicators.note: variously suggests the letters are arranged in some different way
deleted tells us to strike that letter out of the other word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to the word's first letter, where it begins

parts.note: the first letter of expressions

explanation.surface: Something can't be told apart from a range of rude remarks with the first word cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one E out of INDELICATE and rearrange the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are identical are exactly alike, so nobody can tell them apart.

clue.text: Tree pipit eventually spotted near a mountain in Central America

indicators.note: in tells us the assembled letters go inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: CA is the usual abbreviation for Central America

indicators.note: near tells us to place that letter beside the next piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: eventually means in the end, so take the word's final letter

parts.note: the last letter of pipit
an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher finally spots a pipit in a tree near a Central American peak.
explanation.walkthrough: The T goes after A, then ALP follows, and all of it sits between C and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The catalpa is a genus of trees with large heart-shaped leaves and long bean-like pods.

clue.text: A suitable place for curtains?

parts.note: surface reading: somewhere good to hang drapes, like a four-poster bed with its hangings
setter's reading: curtains is slang for the end of life, so this is where someone dies

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's curtains for him' means he is finished or dead; the bed is where that happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The bed a person lies in at the moment of dying is the fitting place for their final curtains.

clue.text: Extremely unpleasant dust storm beginning to die away

indicators.note: away says that letter goes off, removed from the whirlwind word

parts.note: a dust devil is a small whirlwind of dust

indicators.note: beginning points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of die

explanation.surface: A nasty dust storm starting to blow itself out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devil' stands for the dust storm as in 'dust devil'; drop its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil describes something deeply wicked or harmful, well beyond mildly unpleasant.

clue.text: Done when a couple of them get agitated

indicators.note: a couple means two, so keep just the opening pair of letters

parts.note: the first two letters of them
an agitated sea is a rough sea

explanation.surface: Finished as soon as a pair of them start getting worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the word ROUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are through with something you have finished it, so it is done.

clue.text: Run out of fish causing confusion

indicators.note: out of here means taken from, so one letter is removed from the fish

parts.note: the barbel is a freshwater fish with whiskers
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Running out of fish throws the household into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out of fish' reads as an empty larder, but R must be taken out of BARBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Tower of Babel story, a babel is a confused noise of many voices.

clue.text: Unattached princess has dreadful secret

parts.note: Di is Princess Diana

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so these letters are messed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A single royal is hiding a shocking secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess = DI is a crossword staple from Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate or distinct, so not joined or attached to anything else.

clue.text: Part of Arafat's evaluation backed by religious texts

indicators.note: backed says the letters run backwards, from right to left
part of says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An assessment of Yasser Arafat that leans on scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Read arafATS EVAluation, then backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avesta is the sacred book of Zoroastrianism, a collection of holy scripture.

clue.text: Uncovers debris so spread out

indicators.note: spread out means scattered about, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clearing away scattered rubble reveals something.
explanation.definitionFit: To disrobe is to take off clothes, which uncovers the body.

clue.text: Mistaken about girl's top

parts.note: if your guess is out, it is mistaken
C stands for circa, Latin for about
a lass is a girl; the 's joins her to what follows

explanation.surface: Someone has got a young woman's blouse wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a noun for clothing; it is the verb meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To outclass rivals is to be far better than them, to beat or top them.

clue.text: Remarkable note penned by novelist

indicators.note: penned means shut inside an enclosure, so one piece sits within the name

parts.note: Clancy Sigal was an American novelist who lived in London
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A writer jots down a striking comment.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside SIGAL, the surname of the American writer Clancy Sigal.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, signal means notable or striking, as in a signal achievement.

clue.text: Servant girl's back after only a short time

indicators.note: after puts the girl's letter behind the word for only

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of girl
an era is a time; cut short, it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: The maid is back at work after only a brief absence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Servant girl' reads as one phrase, but the definition is Servant alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A butler is the chief manservant of a household, in charge of the wine and the table.

clue.text: Familiar sound of birds circling a short distance above Nelson's head

indicators.note: in a down answer, above puts one piece on top of the next
circling means going around, so the bird sound wraps the distance

parts.note: coo is the soft call of doves and pigeons
mm, a millimetre, is a very short distance

indicators.note: the head of a name is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Nelson

explanation.surface: Pigeons wheel just above the top of Nelson's Column, a well-known sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's Column in London's Trafalgar Square is famous for its pigeons.
explanation.definitionFit: Something common is ordinary and widely known, so it is familiar.

clue.text: What Scrooge had to replace with compassion

parts.note: to change something is to replace it
of in the sense of having, as in a man of means
heart is kindness and compassion

explanation.surface: Scrooge had to swap his meanness for kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's A Christmas Carol, the miser Scrooge becomes generous after the ghosts visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrooge's overnight conversion from miser to benefactor is the classic example of a complete reversal of attitude.

clue.text: A tendency over time to keep soldiers from revolting

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the tendency word spreads around what follows

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the time word holds the soldiers

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Over time an army grew inclined to stop its troops rebelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like rebellion, matching the soldiers, but it means disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abhorrent inspires disgust and loathing, so it is revolting.

clue.text: Entered with authority to go around tax department

indicators.note: going around something means surrounding it, so the expert word encloses the next pieces

parts.note: an ace is an expert, an authority on a subject
a cess is a tax or levy
D is an abbreviation for department

explanation.surface: Someone got in with permission to tour the tax office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entered with authority' reads as the definition, but 'with' only links; a cess is an old word for a local tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To access a place or a computer file is to get into it, so it means entered.

clue.text: May, for instance, abridge article on swindle involving corrupt alderman

indicators.note: in an across answer, on puts the article after the swindle
involving means wrapping in, so the swindle surrounds the councillor's letters

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: corrupt means twisted out of true, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to abridge is to shorten, so the article loses its end

parts.note: the definite article

explanation.surface: Theresa May's report is cut short over a fraud by a crooked councillor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like a person, but it is the month; an alderman is a senior local councillor.
explanation.definitionFit: May is one of the twelve named divisions of the year, an example of a month in the calendar.

clue.text: Very hard to stop Matt getting upset after a refusal

indicators.note: after says the rest follows the refusal

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom
to stop means plugging a gap, so the letter goes in among the others

parts.note: matt paint has a flat finish
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Matt gets terribly upset after being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Not half is an informal British intensifier, so 'not half bad' means very good indeed.

clue.text: Deny grabbing women from a London street

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so the denial word holds the letter

parts.note: to negate is to deny
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Someone denies snatching women off a London road.
explanation.walkthrough: Newgate Street in the City of London is named after the old Newgate Prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate Street is a thoroughfare in the City of London near St Paul's Cathedral.

clue.text: Insist upon getting activists' leader to lock up

indicators.note: in a down answer, upon puts one piece on top of the other
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of activists

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Protest leaders demand a building be secured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock up' looks like imprisoning; it is a lock of hair turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something is to state it firmly and insist on it.

clue.text: Appears as girl's holding court

indicators.note: holding means having within, so the name surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name, plus the 's
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A young woman seems to be holding a royal reception.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of girl's is kept as an S.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a role is to perform it on stage, so an actor who enacts Hamlet appears as him.

clue.text: Acknowledge everyone without rising

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means going upward, so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: w/o is the written abbreviation of without

explanation.surface: Admit that nobody is getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow a point is to admit or concede it, as in 'I'll allow that you're right'.

clue.text: Continued to hedge about following a girl in the dark

indicators.note: following says this part comes after the girl

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: to hedge is to enclose with a hedge, so one word fences in the other

parts.note: was in the sense of carried on existing, remained
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone kept dodging after following a woman through the darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continued' stands for the verb in the sense of remained or carried on, as in 'so it was for years'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught unawares is to be taken by surprise, without knowledge, much like being kept in the dark.

clue.text: Heard beast's cry

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the word is pronounced, not how it is written

parts.note: the whale is a great sea beast

explanation.surface: Someone heard an animal howling.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after beast is 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wail is a long high cry of grief or pain.

clue.text: Power to seize key American bank

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold, so the power word holds the rest

parts.note: sway is power or influence
ALT is a key on a computer keyboard
A is an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A power grab on a major US bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' reads as a noun, but it is the verb meaning to save money.
explanation.definitionFit: To salt away money is to put it aside secretly for the future, just as one banks it.

clue.text: Cell door breached by writer

indicators.note: a breach is a break in a barrier, so the writer gets inside it

parts.note: a gate is a kind of door
the writer of the clue is the setter, who says me

explanation.surface: A prison cell door is forced by an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell door' suggests a jail; the definition is a biological cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamete is a reproductive cell, such as a sperm or egg.

clue.text: Failure of Worcestershire's opener caught by Bradman at slip

indicators.note: caught means held fast, so that letter sits inside the cricketer's name

parts.note: Sir Donald Bradman, the great Australian batsman, was known as the Don

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, like a batting opener

parts.note: the first letter of Worcestershire
to slip is to fall

explanation.surface: A cricket dismissal: a county batsman caught by Bradman fielding at slip.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcestershire is an English county cricket team; slip is a fielding position next to the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a loss of power or success, a ruin or failure.

clue.text: Best to have sex and leave

parts.note: to best someone is to beat them
it is slang for sex

explanation.surface: Advice for a one-night stand: sleep together, then go.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is a slang order to go away, so it means leave.
